assumptions: All cooperating readers and writers use the repository-common coordinator lock.
The local filesystem supplies POSIX flock semantics and atomic file replacement.
SQLite processes use separate connections to one database on a supported local filesystem.
A continuously runnable process is eventually scheduled and a lock holder eventually exits its critical section.
Successful local commits and SQLite transactions have the durability described by the coordinator contract.
The pinned TLC verifier is downloaded successfully and matches its recorded SHA-256 digest.
limitations: TLC explores only the finite constants declared in the six tracked model configurations.
The evidence applies only to the specifications, configurations, invariants, and temporal properties executed by formal/handoffctl/verify.sh.
Implementation tests provide separate correspondence evidence but do not turn bounded model checking into an implementation proof.
Separate clones, network filesystems, non-cooperating writers, and failures outside the documented recovery boundary are excluded.
non_claims: This evidence does not prove the Python implementation correct.
This evidence does not prove correctness of Python, Git, GitHub, SQLite, the operating system, the kernel, or the filesystem.
This evidence does not prove correctness of arbitrary commands executed through handoffctl run.
This evidence does not establish atomicity across power loss, storage loss, or arbitrary process termination.
